bull_bear.body: Dividend INR2.40/share (120% of FV) for FY26. Major working-capital improvement: OCF +INR370cr (vs −INR99cr) via realising long-held receivables; expects further improvement and to stay within sanctioned bank limits (finance cost roughly flat). Rising R&D investment. In-principle board approval to demerge Space/Meteorology/Hydrology business — detailed scheme expected within weeks — to sharpen focus, governance and create clearer shareholder investment propositions.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Govt-driven program timing/delays (budget & priority) — TAM intact but slipping ~2 yrs (FY28–29 → FY30–31).
- Back-ended (rear-ended) 3x growth concentrated in 5–6 programs — execution & qualification gating (Su-30 radar qualify ~FY28, production possibly 2–3 yrs later; BEL flagged Su-30 still in development ~5 yrs).
- JV forex exposure (~$2m provision hit FY26 profit).
- Margin near top end — downside if mix shifts.
- Working-capital intensity rises with volume.
- Unproven proprietary-IP/branded products (timelines "before Diwali" / "by November") — execution-contingent upside, not yet de-risked.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident, long-term, philosophy-heavy (Atim Kabra: "speak less, think long term, deliver"; "only the paranoid survive"). Strong "under-promise" framing — repeatedly told analysts to model lower margins and stressed 3x excludes exports/BEL/IP products ("gravy on top"). Proud re-rating narrative (Tier-1 systems house, DCPP, holy-grail Astra-branded IP) anchored in listed delivered systems. Candid on delays being government-side, not execution-side.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- 3x turnover aspiration rests on just 5–6 programs (QRSAM, Uttam, Su-30 Virupaksha radar, Su-30 Angad EW pod, JV/ARC, electronic mines) — exports, BEL programs and Astra-owned-IP products are all EXCLUDED upside.
- "Virupaksha"/Uttam radar AAAU is a DRDO program where Astra develops the active antenna array unit; Uttam order to be placed by HAL (not DRDO directly).
- Su-30 EW pod ("Angad") — Astra is one of two selected DCPPs.
- Astra-owned, Astra-branded IP products (complete IP with Astra) to launch "before Diwali"; first NCNC demo this quarter — entirely outside guidance.
- Demerger of Space/Met/Hydrology in-principle approved — scheme in weeks; reshapes the ~16% space segment into a standalone vehicle.
- Photonics (optical-domain) radar and GPR developed with startup partners; digital-array radar subsystems already delivered to DRDO.
- MMIC: zero supply issues; pivoting from purely captive to also selling chips to domestic + international players.
- Export "exports" line is largely sales to own JV ARC (co-developed RF for Rafael SDRs), not third-party — high value-add.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- The LEAP framework's "Accretiveness" pillar centres on enhancing Return on Equity, profitability and margin improvement, with focus on working capital efficiency, free cash flow generation and "financial discipline and sustainable value creation for shareholders".
- Working capital metrics improved in FY26: debtor days 216 (FY25: 273), inventory days 193 (FY25: 213), creditor days 36 (FY25: 27), and cash conversion cycle 374 days (FY25: 459).
- Standalone balance sheet shows current borrowings falling to Rs 224 Cr at Mar-26 from Rs 379 Cr at Mar-25 while non-current borrowings rose to Rs 63 Cr from Rs 39 Cr; cash and cash equivalents rose to Rs 165 Cr from Rs 21 Cr.
- Standalone equity attributable to owners rose to Rs 1,272 Cr at Mar-26 from Rs 1,071 Cr at Mar-25; the deck states no dividend policy or payout.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Exclusive focus on defence and space electronics with no consumer exposure - the AR states the product portfolio is comprised solely of electronics for Defence and Space applications.
- Entrenched position with strategic-sector buyers: key customers are government agencies, DPSUs, public sector enterprises and institutional clients, a customer set with high qualification and switching barriers.
- Long operating history in a design-led business - incorporated 13-09-1991 and presenting its 35th Annual Report, covering design, development and manufacturing rather than assembly alone.
- Reaffirmed credit standing: CRISIL A/Positive on long-term bank facilities and corporate credit rating, and CRISIL A1 on short-term bank facilities.
- Skilled engineering base of 1,684 permanent employees (1,880 including non-permanent) with no worker cadre, consistent with a design and systems-integration model.
- Assured non-financial reporting - BRSR Core disclosures carried Reasonable Assurance from Intertek India Private Limited.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data privacy and cyber security exposure in RF/microwave and digital electronics products — The only material issue the BRSR table classifies as a Risk with NEGATIVE financial implications. The company states that in RF/Microwave/Digital electronics, hardware products and associated software can harbor security gaps that may threaten consumer data security, and that a failure to devise a comprehensive methodology to detect such vulnerabilities would place customer data at risk and undermine the customer relationship. Mitigation is a Cyber Risk Management framework overseen by the Information Technology & Security Committee and the Risk Management Committee, with controlled data access, encryption and stakeholder education. Structurally acute given a defence and space customer base.
- Corporate governance risk — The second material issue classified as a Risk in the BRSR table, with the company noting it is assessed on key governance areas such as ownership structure, board remuneration and accounting practices. The bundle text is truncated mid-row, so the stated mitigation and financial implication for this row are not readable. Board composition changes support the concern being live: two independent directors ceased during FY26 (22 May 2025 and 26 June 2025), two joined on 22 May 2025, and the CFO position turned over three times inside the year.
- Occupational health and safety hazards across manufacturing units — The company runs a formal OHS management system across its units and Head Office covering routine and non-routine activities, with hazards scored on Likelihood x Severity, classes of Unacceptable or Needs Correction (L x S of 5 to 25) prioritised for corrective action, a designated Emergency Response Team, and 100% of plants and offices assessed for health and safety practices and working conditions. Reported outcomes for FY 2025-26 are nil across LTIFR, total recordable work-related injuries, fatalities and high-consequence injuries, so the risk is managed rather than currently crystallised.
- Product design and technology obsolescence in RF and microwave technology — Listed as material issue 1 and framed by the company as an OPPORTUNITY with positive implications, not a risk, but structurally it is a technology-cycle exposure: the company itself notes that competitive advantage, customer loyalty and market growth depend on staying at the forefront of technological advancements in RF and microwave technology. No mitigation approach is stated because the row is classified as an opportunity.
- Talent retention and employee satisfaction — Listed as material issue 2 and framed as an opportunity with positive implications. For a design-and-development-led defence electronics business with no worker cadre, retention of engineering staff is a structural dependency; the company cites work-life balance, career development, competitive compensation and work environment as the levers that drive morale, productivity and retention. No complaints on working conditions or health and safety were filed in FY 2025-26 or FY 2024-25.
- Supply chain sustainability and supplier dependence — Listed as material issue 3, again framed as an opportunity. The company notes that firms actively managing supply-chain impacts through standards, monitoring and supplier engagement may be better positioned to protect shareholder value in the long run, implying that unmanaged supplier exposure is the corresponding downside. No mitigation approach is stated because the row is classified as an opportunity.
- Energy management and clean technology transition — Listed as material issue 4 and classified as an opportunity with positive implications: the company links reduced energy consumption and integration of renewable energy sources to lower operational costs and carbon footprint, and ties clean technology to reputation and market position. The residual exposure is energy cost and the pace of the transition rather than a flagged risk.

business.body:

business.body:
- Self-described as having a "proven track record of making high value-added SYSTEMS, RF and Microwave Super Components and Sub-Systems", engaged in India's space program for 25 years, and having developed 35 Radars, 25 Satellites and 15 Strategic Programs till date.
- Claims to be "one of the few private sector players in India that has the capability to develop and supply GaN & GaAs MMIC products up to 40 GHz", and is participating in multiple MAKE-II programs of the IAF and Indian Army for various Radar Systems.
- Revenue is concentrated in government/PSU defence: FY26 standalone revenue by customer is DRDO 28.2%, BEL & other DPSUs 22.7%, IMD / Met Dept 18.0%, Exports (via ARC + Aelius) 11.9%, ISRO / SAC 6.4%, Private Customers 3.0% and BSF 0.3%.
- Order book by order type as on 30 June 2026 is led by Production at Rs 1,417 Cr (65.7%), with Development Rs 308 Cr (14.3%), AMC/Service Rs 258 Cr (12.0%) and Export Rs 173 Cr (8.0%), in the order the deck lists them.
- Historical order book has roughly kept pace with scale: Rs 1,561 Cr (FY21), Rs 1,551 Cr (FY22), Rs 1,544 Cr (FY23), Rs 1,956 Cr (FY24), Rs 1,952 Cr (FY25) and Rs 2,141 Cr (FY26).

business.body: The company designs, develops and manufactures RF and microwave systems, sub-systems and components, together with navigational, meteorological, geophysical and related instruments. outlook.body:
- Reduce the environmental footprint through renewable self-generation - solar photovoltaic systems have been installed across offices and manufacturing facilities with a cumulative installed capacity of nearly 1 MW, described as supporting a transition towards cleaner energy and reduced reliance on fossil-fuel-based electricity.
- Operate manufacturing effluent handling on Zero Liquid Discharge principles, with complete recycling and reuse of wastewater, treated sludge used for landscaping and gardening, and continuous monitoring to prevent any liquid discharge outside the premises.
- Manage waste through a documented framework across all manufacturing facilities and offices, routing e-waste and hazardous waste exclusively through certified and licensed vendors, with landfilling and incineration reported at nil.
- Pursue continuous facility-level resource-efficiency and safety projects - STP water pipelines to garden areas, solar water heaters in the canteen, gas bank centralisation, earth-pit renovation and ventilation upgrades - rather than a single large sustainability programme.
- Contribute to afforestation and biodiversity through participation in programmes such as Telangana Haritha Haram, and reduce commuting emissions by providing shared transportation for employees.

outlook.body: The routed capex_expansion sections carry no capacity, commissioning, ramp-up, debottlenecking or project narrative. The Management Discussion and Analysis extract routed here is in fact Directors'-Report boilerplate (dividend policy link, transfer to reserves, credit rating, stock-exchange listing, subsidiary/associate statement, board meeting count, Directors' Responsibility Statement) and contains no expansion content. The only structural changes disclosed are corporate-entity events rather than physical expansion: Astra Foundation was converted into Astra Private Limited on 12 March 2025 and struck off from the Register of Companies on 16 September 2025, and Bhavyabhanu Electronics Private Limited was renamed Astra Defence Technologies Private Limited on 18 November 2025 following a change in the company's main objects. The Chairman/MD extract routed here is BRSR Principle 1 and Principle 2 material, whose only capex-related statement is the leadership indicator that R&D and capital expenditure investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were 0% of total R&D and 0% of total capex in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.

deepdive.thesis: Three-decade RF/microwave house re-rating itself from "Tier-2 subsystem supplier" to a Tier-1, IP-driven systems manufacturer and a DCPP (development-cum-production-partner) for strategic national programs. FY26 delivered turnover INR1,157cr (per guidance), 33%+ EBITDA margin, and a dramatic working-capital turnaround (OCF +INR370cr vs −INR99cr). Standalone order book INR2,141cr (consolidated ~INR2,600cr) + ~INR1,600cr+ bookable in FY27. Mgmt aspires to ~triple turnover in ~4.5–5.5 yrs (by ~FY30–31) on just 5–6 programs (QRSAM, Uttam, Su-30 Virupaksha radar, Su-30 Angad EW pod, ARC/JV, electronic mines) — explicitly excluding exports, BEL programs and future Astra-owned-IP/branded products (multiple to launch "before Diwali"). In-principle board approval to demerge Space/Meteorology/Hydrology business.

open.item: Concluded negotiations for INR400 crores plus orders expected to be booked in Q3 FY26.
FY26 order inflow guidance of INR1,300-1,400 crores; ~INR260 crores booked to date, confident of booking ~INR1,100 crores more by March 2026.
Clear visibility of INR1,300-1,500 crores worth of orders to book in FY26 (domestic + export).
Expecting INR900-1,000 crores of radar segment orders in FY26 (part of INR1,300-1,500 cr total).
Concluded PNC of INR300 crores more orders expected to be received in next couple of months (on top of FY26-end order book of INR2,141 crores standalone).
QRSAM: receiving small FOPM (first-of-production-model) quantities now; main orders expected within 3-4 months after BEL gets its contract (expected ~June).
Uttam radar contract negotiations with HAL at final stage; order expected sometime in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Multiple Astra-owned-IP, Astra-branded products/solutions for India and global markets to hit market this FY, hopefully before Diwali; first NCNC demo planned within the quarter.
Reaffirming FY27 top line growth of 15%-20%, targeting sales of INR1,300-1,400 crores.
Clear visibility of approximately INR1,600 crores plus orders to be booked in FY27 (~25% R&D, balance production).
ARC JV expected to deliver top line of over INR600 crores in FY27 with minimum 50% growth in both orders and sales; ~INR20 crores+ share of profit (EBITDA 18-20%).
Expect to sustain current margins (~55% gross); management flags this is likely the top end, factor slightly lower on margins.
Clear visibility of at least 20% growth in order book for FY27.
Own Astra SAT-1 satellite to be put in space in less than 24 months, intended to be revenue-accretive.
Su-30 Virupaksha AAAU development to complete in next 2-3 months; radar qualification expected in FY28, production orders 2-3 years thereafter.
FY28 turnover expected around INR1,650 crores (plus/minus INR50 crores), adding Uttam radar revenues.
FY29 turnover expected close to INR2,000 crores, adding Su-30 upgrade revenues.
FY30 turnover expected around INR2,250-2,500 crores with all programs in full production.
Structurally positioned to nearly triple turnover over ~4.5-5.5 years (by FY30-FY31), based on 5-6 major programs.
Total addressable opportunity of ~INR28,000 crores remains intact but shifted from FY28-FY29 to FY30-FY31 due to program delays.
